description:
FILED s521d (Opus 5.5, 2026-10-18) from the #3518 probes (scratch/s521d/pr/dot.pl):
    open my $fh, '<', $0; my $l = <$fh>; $. = 20;
    { local $. = 30; } print "$.\n";   # perl 30   PCL 20
    close $fh; print "$.\n";           # perl 0    PCL 20
perl's `local $.` localizes only the CURRENT-HANDLE pointer (PL_last_in_gv) -- the bare `local $.;` spelling already lowers to p-local-dot, which does that, but `local $. = N` lowers to a whole-box `(let (($. (p-box-for-local N))) ...)` that saves and restores the VALUE.  And close of the current handle resets its IoLINES to 0 while the handle stays the one $. reads.  PRE-EXISTING (68aeebf5 the same); LOW.  Fix shape: route `local $. = N` through p-local-dot + the assignment; close zeroes the handle's counter in *p-fh-lines*.
subject: `local $. = N` with a handle current restores the OLD line count where perl keeps the handle's new count, and `close` of the last-read handle leaves $. at its count where perl reads 0
